history.period: Treta Yuga (legendary); modern riverfront development inaugurated by CM Nitish Kumar in 2024
history.summary: Simaria Ghat is a major Ganga pilgrimage ghat in Begusarai district (near Barauni, by the Rajendra Pul) - a ghat complex, not a single temple building. Tradition makes it the tapobhumi of King Janaka of Mithila, who is said to have started the famous Kalpavas Mela here in the Treta Yuga; devotees still observe the month-long Kalpavas ritual in Kartik month, and one local tradition links the spot to the distribution of amrit after the Samudra Manthan (all legend - flagged). The nearby Simaria village is the birthplace of poet Ramdhari Singh Dinkar. Bihar's first riverfront development on this ghat was inaugurated by CM Nitish Kumar (2024), and the annual two-day Simaria Festival with Dev Deepawali has run since 2011. Also the CSV town 'Begusarai' is approximate: the ghat is at Simaria, near Barauni in Barauni block, some distance from Begusarai town. Coordinates are approximate (verify).

name: Simaria Ghat Temple
town_description: Simaria is a riverside village on the Ganga near Barauni in Begusarai district of Bihar, overlooked by the Rajendra Pul rail-cum-road bridge. It is a major Hindu pilgrimage centre, famous for the month-long Kartik Kalpavas Mela at Simaria Ghat, and is the birthplace of the Hindi poet Ramdhari Singh Dinkar.
